entry.name: jit.matrix
entry.description: The jit.matrix object is a named matrix which may be used for data storage and retrieval, resampling, and matrix type and planecount conversion operations.

attributes.name: adapt
attributes.digest: Matrix adaptation flag
attributes.description: Matrix adaptation flag (default = 0 if matrix arguments are present, otherwise 1) When the flag is set, theobject will adapt to the incoming matrix planecount, type, and dimensions.

messages.name: (drag)
messages.digest: Load a compatible media file
messages.description: Drag and drop a compatible media file onto the object to load it.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Output the currently stored matrix
messages.description: Outputs the currently stored matrix.

messages.name: clear
messages.digest: Set all matrix values to zero
messages.description: Sets all matrix values to zero.

messages.name: exportimage
messages.digest: Export the current frame as an image file
messages.description: Export the current frame as an image file with the name specified by the first argument. The second argument sets the file type (default = png). Available file types are,, and.You can use the Max Preferences tofor PNG images.

messages.name: exportmovie
messages.digest: Export a matrix as a movie
messages.description: Exports a matrix as a movie. Themessage takes an optional argument to specify a file name. If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file.See theobject for information on thearguments and their default values.

messages.name: exprfill
messages.digest: Evaluate an expression to fill the matrix
messages.description: Evaluatesto fill the matrix. If aargument is provided, the expression is applied to a single plane. Otherwise, it is applied to all planes in the matrix. Seefor more information on expressions. Unlike theobject, there is no support for providing multiple expressions to fill multiple planes at once with different expressions. Call this method multiple times once for each plane you wish to fill.

messages.name: fillplane
messages.digest: Fill a plane with a specified value
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer that specifies a plane number and a value, will fill the specified plane with the single value.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
messages.description: Sets all cells to the value specified byand output the data. Value is specified as a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions ().

messages.name: getcell
messages.digest: Report cell values
messages.description: Sends the value(s) in the cell specified byout the right outlet of the object as a list in the form.......

messages.name: importmovie
messages.digest: Import a movie into the matrix
messages.description: Imports a movie into the matrix. If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file. Theargument may be used to set a time offset for the movie being imported (the default is 0).

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
messages.description: Sets all cells to the value specified byand output the data. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions ().

messages.name: jit_gl_texture
messages.digest: Copy a texture to the matrix
messages.description: Copies the texture specified byto the matrix.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
messages.description: Sets all cells to the value specified byand output the data. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions ().

messages.name: op
messages.digest: Performoperations on the matrix
messages.description: The word, followed by the name of aobject operator and a set of values, is equivalent to including aobject with the specified operator set as an attribute and thisobject specified as the output matrix. The additionalarguments may either be a matrix name or a constant. If only one value argument is provided, this matrix is considered both the output and the left operand. For example, "op + foo bar" is equivalent to the operation thismatrix = foo + bar, and "op * 0.5" is equivalent to the operation thismatrix = thismatrix * 0.5.

messages.name: read
messages.digest: Read Jitter binary data files (.jxf)
messages.description: Reads Jitter binary data files (.jxf) into a matrix set. If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file.

messages.name: setall
messages.digest: Set all cells to a value
messages.description: Sets all cells to the value specified by. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions ().

messages.name: setcell
messages.digest: Set a cell to a specified value
messages.description: Sets the cell specified byto the value specified by. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions (). The optional argumentscan be used to specify a plane. If a plane is specified,should be a single number, otherwise it should be a list of numbers of size.

messages.name: setcell1d
messages.digest: Set a 1-dimensional cell to a specified value
messages.description: The word, followed by a number specifying ancoordinate and a list of values, is similar to themessage but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (1) is fixed.

messages.name: setcell2d
messages.digest: Set a 2-dimensional cell to specified values
messages.description: The word, followed by a pair of numbers specifyingandcoordinates and a list of values, is similar to themessage but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (2) is fixed.

messages.name: setcell3d
messages.digest: Set a 3-dimensional cell to specified values
messages.description: The word, followed by three numbers specifying,, andcoordinates and a list of values, is similar to themessage but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (3) is fixed.

messages.name: setplane1d
messages.digest: Set a cell in a plane to a value (1d, no val token)
messages.description: The word, followed by a number specifying ancoordinate, a number specifying a plane, and a value, is similar to themessage but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (1) is fixed, or use the "plane" token to specify which plane to set.

messages.name: setplane2d
messages.digest: Set a cell in a plane to a value (2d, no val token)
messages.description: The word, followed by a pair of numbers specifyingandcoordinates, a number specifying a plane, and a value, is similar to themessage but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (2) is fixed, or use the "plane" token to specify which plane to set.

messages.name: setplane3d
messages.digest: Set a cell in a plane to a value (3d, no val token)
messages.description: The word, followed by three numbers specifying,, andcoordinates, a number specifying a plane, and a value, is similar to themessage but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (1) is fixed, or use the "plane" token to specify which plane to set.

messages.name: val
messages.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
messages.description: Sets all cells to the value specified by. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions () and outputs the data.

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write matrix set as a Jitter binary data file (.jxf)
messages.description: Writes matrix set as a Jitter binary data file (.jxf). If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file.
